results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around The Jolly Balloon Man, Sewer-veillance Cam and Bloom Tender.
results.text:
I submitted a 4-color (G/W/R/U) Balloon Man brew. It borrows the green ramp shell of Standard's Aang deck.

**The plan:** Llanowar Elves, Bloom Tender and Sewer-veillance Cam put permanents of four colors on the battlefield. That lets Bloom Tender tap for about 4 mana by itself from turn 3. The Jolly Balloon Man has haste, and for {1} it makes a hasty copy of any creature you control. Early on, copying Bloom Tender turns that {1} into about 4 more mana. Later, copying Craterhoof Behemoth gives every attacker a second +X/+X-and-trample bonus. Two Hoof bodies swinging with trample deal far more than 20 damage around turn 5.

**What each requested card does:**
- **Bloom Tender** is the mana engine. Its Vivid ability makes one mana of each color among your permanents, so it's worth about 4 mana here, and its copies are worth the same.
- **Sewer-veillance Cam** costs U and has flash. It counts as the blue permanent, and both its enter and leave triggers can untap Balloon Man for an extra copy. They can also tap down a blocker on the kill turn.
- **The Jolly Balloon Man** copies things:
  - Bloom Tender for mana
  - Craterhoof for the kill
  - Explosive Prodigy, to deal its 4 damage to another creature
  - Brightglass Gearhulk, to search for two more one-drops. Cam is one of the cards it can fetch.
- **Backup copiers and untappers:** Forensic Researcher and Marvin, Murderous Mimic. Marvin copies the abilities of your other creatures, so it acts as both a second Balloon Man and a second Bloom Tender.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. A 5-color Vivid deck that copies Shimmercreep to drain the opponent.
2. A Jeskai tempo deck using Cam with Glamermite and Flash Thompson.
3. The green ramp package from the Aang deck, with Craterhoof and Nature's Rhythm.

I chose the third because copying Craterhoof wins in one turn. I also looked for an infinite loop. Every untapper in Standard gives only one untap per copy, and each copy costs {1}, so the deck has no infinite combo, just big turns.

**Things to know:**
- Badgermole Cub is banned now, so the ramp package runs without it.
- On the play, you'll have Balloon Man plus Craterhoof or Nature's Rhythm by turn 5 in about 35% of games. That figure doesn't count Gearhulk or Rhythm searching for the missing piece. Prodigy and Gearhulk copies keep you in the game when the kill pieces don't show up.
- The sideboard is mostly aimed at Prowess and the other top decks: Pawpatch Formation, Sear, Abrade, Disdainful Stroke and Rest in Peace.

winLine.does: Turn 1 ramp, adds a green permanent for Vivid
Turn 2; once blue, red/white and green permanents are out it taps for 3-4 mana by itself
One-mana flash blue permanent, which turns on a fourth Vivid color; its enter/leave triggers untap Balloon Man or Bloom Tender, or tap a blocker
Turn 3, haste: pay {1}, tap to make a hasty copy of Bloom Tender that taps for ~4 mana, then sorcery-speed copy engine for the rest of the game
Cast off Bloom Tender + lands (or fetched by Nature's Rhythm); haste, ETB gives all creatures +X/+X and trample
Pay {1} to copy Craterhoof: a second hasty, flying Hoof trigger stacks another +X/+X on every attacker. Two Hoof bodies swing for well over 20 with trample

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Dáin's Company, Dwarven Mauler and Kíli the Resourceful.
results.text:
This is Boros (red-white) Dwarf Equipment aggro, labeled a brew. No published list in the last 400 days plays these three cards together, and none of them has shown up in recent results yet. So this deck is built from the card pool, not copied from a proven list.

**Directions I considered:**
1. Pure Dwarf Voltron (one creature carrying lots of Equipment).
2. A Dwarf/Equipment core plus the cheap burn package from the menu's Boros Aggro deck.
3. Going wide with Fíli the Pathfinder and The Lonely Mountain making 2/2 Dwarf tokens.

I chose #2. Dwarf Voltron with no interaction loses to the Prowess and Elementals creatures. Four copies of Burst Lightning clear blockers and still let the Dwarves and Equipment drive the deck. I also checked Boros Weapons, but it's an artifact-control deck rather than an Equipment deck, so I didn't borrow from it.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Dwarven Mauler** is the turn-1 body that carries Equipment. Its equip discount of 2 makes Leyline Axe cost 1 to equip, and Fireshrieker and Lost Jitte cost 0.
- **Kíli the Resourceful** draws a card each turn a Dwarf or Equipment enters (once per turn). With 3+ artifacts or legendary cards in play (its "storied" condition), your first equip each turn is free. With 9 legendary creatures, 4 legendary Equipment and Dáin Ironfoot's Axe token, that's easy to reach.
- **Dáin's Company** looks at the top 4 cards for a Dwarf or Equipment, and gets lifelink when you control another Dwarf.

**The plan:** Turn 1 Mauler. If Leyline Axe is in your opening hand it starts the game on the battlefield, so on turn 2 you play Kíli and equip Mauler for 1. That makes Mauler a 3/2 with double strike and trample, hitting for 6 a turn. Dáin's Company, Giott and Dáin Ironfoot keep Dwarves and Equipment coming and give out more double strike. Mjölnir's 4 damage when it enters kills a blocker, and it doubles the damage of the legendary Dwarf carrying it. The target kill is turn 5.

**Odds:** You'll see Mauler or Kíli by turn 3 about 75% of the time, Equipment about 83%, and both about 61% (before counting Dáin's Company's digging). The exact best-case line, with every card drawn by turn 5, only happens 0.3% of the time. The deck relies on having many interchangeable Dwarves and Equipment, not one fixed sequence.

**Mana:** 22 lands (18 red sources, 17 white). Boros Aggro decks average about 23.4 lands, but this curve is lower (average mana value 2.16).

**Sideboard:**
- Sear and Seam Rip for Prowess and Selesnya Offense.
- Magebane Lizard for decks casting lots of spells.
- Ghost Vacuum for graveyard decks.
- Bofur and Thorin, Mountain-king for control decks.

winLine.does: Starts the game on the battlefield from the opening hand (a free artifact toward storied)
Turn 1 Dwarf; equip costs targeting it are 2 less, so Leyline Axe's equip 3 costs just 1
Turn 2: draws a card off the next Dwarf/Equipment; Mauler gets Axe for 1 and swings as a 3/2 double strike trampler (6 damage)
Turn 3 Dwarf (lifelink next to other Dwarves) digs 4 cards for another Dwarf or Equipment and triggers Kíli's draw
Turn 4: ETB deals 4 to a blocker; with storied (Axe + Kíli + Mjölnir) Kíli's free first equip puts it on a worthy legend, which doubles its damage
Clears a blocker or finishes the last 2 points after 6+6 double-strike swings

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Greedy Freebooter, The Sackville-Bagginses and Umbral Collar Zealot.
results.text:
I built a brew called **Rakdos Sacrifice**. It's a heavily black deck that sacrifices its own creatures for value, built around Umbral Collar Zealot, The Sackville-Bagginses and Greedy Freebooter. No published list has played these three together, so it's untested.

**The plan:** Greedy Freebooter, Infestation Sage, Bloodghast and Bitterbloom Bearer give you cheap bodies to sacrifice. Zealot is a free, instant-speed outlet, so you can sacrifice them whenever you want. Sackville turns every token you sacrifice into 1 life lost for your opponent. That includes Treasures, so even sacrificing a Treasure for mana counts.

- **Totentanz:** makes a Rat whenever a nontoken creature of yours dies, so each death leaves another token behind.
- **Popular Egotist:** drains 1 more on every sacrifice. With Sackville out, each token you sacrifice drains 2.
- **Garna:** drains 1 more whenever one of your creatures dies outside combat.
- **Bloodghast:** comes back every time you play a land, so you don't run out of things to sacrifice.
- **Requiting Hex:** its optional cost can put a -1/-1 counter on Freebooter. Freebooter dies, so you also get a Treasure and a scry.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Orzhov (white-black):** Vito, Syr Vondam and Tolls of War.
2. **Golgari (green-black):** a graveyard deck with Insidious Roots and Badgermole Cub, which is where Zealot currently shows up in results.
3. **Rakdos (red-black):** Totentanz, Egotist and Garna, plus the Bloodghast package and red-black lands from the menu's Mardu Discard deck.

I chose Rakdos because its payoffs (Totentanz, Egotist, Garna) trigger on the exact things these three cards do: tokens, Treasures and creatures dying. The other two would have used your cards as supporting pieces rather than the main engine.

**Honest odds:**
- The calculator puts drawing all six cards of the listed win line by turn 6 at only 0.8%. That number is misleading, because the deck doesn't need those specific cards.
- Without mulligans, you have at least one outlet or drain card (Zealot, Sackville or Egotist) by turn 3 about 83% of the time. You have one of those plus a creature to sacrifice about 76% of the time.

**Mana:** 22 lands with 14 red sources, which is enough for Garna's two red. The deck check flagged that Mardu Discard lists run far more white sources. I ignored that because this deck has no white cards.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in the field:
- **Prowess and other aggro:** Burst Lightning and Abrade
- **Landfall and Selesnya Offense:** Deathmark
- **Control and Dimir decks:** Duress and Strategic Betrayal
- **Graveyard decks:** Ghost Vacuum
- **General removal:** Shoot the Sheriff

winLine.does: Turn 1 one-drop that leaves a Treasure token (plus scry 1) when it dies
Turn 2 free sac outlet: sacrifice creatures, Treasures and other tokens at instant speed, surveil 1 each
Turn 3: every nontoken creature that dies makes a 1/1 Rat; sac Freebooter to Zealot for Treasure + Rat
Turn 4: ETB sacrifices the Rat (draw + new Treasure); from then on every token sacrificed (Rats, Treasures, Faeries, Insects) makes the opponent lose 1
Adds another drain of 1 (and 1 life for you) on every sacrifice, so each token sac drains 2 alongside Sackville
Comes back from the graveyard every time you play a land, so you never run out of sac fodder; drains and attacks finish the opponent

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Gideon's Memorial, Solitary Cell and Ajani Unrelenting.
results.text:
I built **Boros Superfriends**, a red-white planeswalker deck (a brew, 60 cards with a 15-card sideboard). No published list in any format plays these three cards together, so this hasn't been tested in tournaments.

**The plan:** Gideon's Memorial comes down on turn 2. Its mana can only cast planeswalkers, which lets you play Chandra on turn 3, Elspeth on turn 4 and Ajani Unrelenting on turn 5. Solitary Cell exiles an early threat with mana value 3 or less. Later it turns spare legendary cards (extra walkers, Way of the Pyromancer) into fresh draws.

Ajani is the engine. Every loyalty ability you activate, on any walker, makes a 2/2 Cadet. Elspeth doubles each token you make. Memorial gives your tokens +1/+0 and vigilance. Ajani's −3 deals 4 damage to every creature except your tokens, so it wipes their board and leaves your army standing. Then his +1 gives the army haste and pushes for the win.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Boros walkers (chosen).** 13 planeswalkers, 2 Way of the Pyromancer (each one also creates a Jace walker, another ability to activate), and cheap removal borrowed from the Azorius Control package (Seam Rip, Get Lost, Erode, Day of Judgment).
2. **Jeskai control with counterspells.** Ajani would just be the finisher. Memorial would mostly be wasted, since its mana only casts walkers.
3. **Boros token aggro** with Voice of Victory. It uses Memorial's +1/+0, but Ajani's 6 mana is too slow for an aggro deck.

I went with the walker build because it's the only one where all three cards do their full job: Memorial only pays for planeswalkers, Ajani gets stronger with every extra walker, and Cell needs spare legendary cards to discard.

**Things to know:**
- **Odds:** Memorial is in your opening hand plus first draws about 57% of the time by turn 2, and you see a planeswalker by turn 4 about 93% of the time. Having *every* piece of the exact winning sequence by turn 7 is rare (about 4% of games). Realistically, the deck wins by stacking whatever walkers it draws behind its removal, not by assembling one fixed combo.
- **Mana:** 24 lands with 19 white and 18 red sources. The deck checker's only flag was that it has no blue sources compared to Azorius Control. That doesn't apply here, since I took only that deck's removal.
- **Choices I made:** I left out Clarion Conqueror even though it's popular in the format, because it turns off your own planeswalkers' abilities. Day of Judgment also kills your tokens, so I kept just 2 in the main deck as an emergency answer to fast creature decks, like Landfall, that hit before your walkers are online.

winLine.does: Turn 2: taps for one extra mana that can only be spent on planeswalker spells, and gives creature tokens +1/+0 and vigilance
Turn 3: exiles the opponent's best permanent with mana value 3 or less. Later it pays {1} and discards a spare legendary card (extra walkers, Way of the Pyromancer) to draw a card
Turn 4 (5 mana with Memorial): +1 makes Soldiers. Her token doubling means every token created after this comes in twice
Turn 5 (6 mana with Memorial): every loyalty ability you activate, from any walker, makes a 2/2 Cadet, so 2 Cadets with Elspeth out. -3 deals 4 to every creature except your tokens
Another walker to activate each turn: its +1 makes a Kithkin (2 with Elspeth) and also sets off Ajani Unrelenting's Cadet trigger
Following turn: +1 gives the token army +1/+0 and haste. With Memorial's +1/+0 and Elspeth doubling, the 3-power Cadets attack for lethal

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Jeskai Revelation, Inevitable Defeat and Tablet of Discovery.
results.text:
I built a 4-color control deck: Jeskai (white, blue, red) with a light black splash. It's a brew. The game plan is to answer threats early with Lightning Helix, Firebending Lesson, Get Lost, Sear and No More Lies. Then, from about turn 5 or 6, cast Inevitable Defeat (an exile that can't be countered, plus a 3-life drain) and Jeskai Revelation (bounce, 4 damage, two prowess Monks, draw two, gain 4) at the end of the opponent's turn. The Monks, The Wandering Emperor, Teferi, and the damage from Revelation, Defeat and Helix close the game, aiming for about turn 8.

**Where it comes from:** I looked up which real decks run these three cards together. The only results were 135 Standard "4C Control" lists. In those decks Tablet of Discovery has two jobs: it lets you play the card it mills, and it taps for RR toward instants. That RR pays the red and one generic mana of Revelation's {4}{U}{R}{W}, so you can cast it a turn early.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Port the Standard 4C Control plan into Pioneer** (chosen). I added No More Lies, Consult the Star Charts, Supreme Verdict and The Wandering Emperor from the UW Control package on your menu.
2. **The 5-color Niv-Mizzet shell.** Up the Beanstalk would draw off Revelation, and Bring to Light could fetch Defeat. But it needs green mana dorks that make Tablet pointless.
3. **A Jeskai spells/tempo deck in the style of Izzet Prowess.** Too low to the ground for seven-mana spells.

I picked the first because it's the only one where all three cards do what they actually do in real decks.

**Mana:** Black is only for the 4 Defeats. It comes from Raffine's Tower, Xander's Lounge, Godless Shrine, Gloomlake Verge, Mana Confluence and Multiversal Passage. Great Hall of the Biblioplex also makes any color for instants and sorceries. The deck check passed against UW Control's numbers, with 26 lands plus 4 Tablets.

**Odds:** You draw at least one Tablet by turn 6 on the play about 60% of the time, and the same for Revelation. Seeing both happens about 35% of the time. Those figures leave out the extra cards from Consult and Stock Up, so the real odds are better. The submission tool reported 0.3% for having every card in the win line by turn 8. That number requires drawing all seven cards in the line, not what the deck actually needs to win.

**Sideboard:** It targets the top decks in the field:
- Rest in Peace for Greasefang and Phoenix
- Fire Magic and Sear for the two Prowess decks
- Dovin's Veto and Mystical Dispute for UW Control and Lotus Field
- Beza, an extra Verdict, an extra Get Lost and an extra Emperor for the midrange decks

winLine.does: Turn 3: mills a card you may play this turn, then taps for RR toward instants, so you can hold up 5+ mana on turn 4 and cast Revelation a turn or two early
Early on, kills an aggressive creature and gains 3 life to stabilize against the prowess decks
Uncounterable instant that exiles their best threat (Sheoldred, Parhelion, Greasefang, a planeswalker), drains them for 3 and gains you 3
Uncounterable sweeper that clears the board when they flood it
At their end step, with Tablet mana: bounce a threat, 4 damage to a creature or their face, two 1/1 prowess Monks, draw 2, gain 4
Flashed in at end of turn to make Samurai or pump the Monks, building the clock while No More Lies protects it
Draws a card each turn and untaps lands to keep up counters. The tokens and Revelation/Defeat/Helix reach damage finish the game

results.prompt: Brew me a Pioneer deck built around Tolarian Terror, Bushwhack and Eddymurk Crab.
results.text:
I built a Temur (blue-red-green) spells deck, and it's a brew. No published list in the last 400 days runs all three of your cards together, and Bushwhack and Tolarian Terror have never shown up in the same deck either.

**The plan:** Cast 1-mana cheap spells (Consider, Opt, Sleight of Hand, Bushwhack, Fiery Impulse, Burst Lightning, Spell Pierce) to fill your graveyard with instants and sorceries. Tolarian Terror and Eddymurk Crab each cost 1 less for every instant or sorcery card there, so a 5/5 often comes down for UU (two blue mana) on turn 3. Bushwhack has two jobs:
- **Early:** it finds a basic land, which fixes your third color and puts a sorcery in the graveyard.
- **Later:** it makes a 5/5 fight a creature, so it works as 1-mana removal. Ram Through does the same thing at instant speed (5 damage with a 5/5).

**One correction to the win line I submitted:** the Crab step there is garbled. If you flash the Crab in on your opponent's turn, it enters tapped. Its "tap two creatures" ability is best used by casting it on your own turn before combat, so it taps their two blockers and both 5/5s hit. Flash is mainly for ambushing an attacker or dodging sorcery-speed removal. Two 5/5s attacking ends the game around turn 6.

**The three directions I considered:**
1. **Simic (blue-green):** Stubborn Denial and Ram Through, but almost no cheap removal.
2. **Sultai (blue-black-green):** borrowing Fatal Push and Thoughtseize from the Golgari and Dimir decks.
3. **Temur, borrowing the cheap red removal and cantrips from the Izzet decks.**

I chose Temur because Fiery Impulse and Burst Lightning are 1-mana removal that also fill the graveyard. Prowess decks are about 18% of the field, and those spells keep you alive until the 5/5s land.

**Other cards:** Stormchaser's Talent (an Izzet staple in the current results) is an early creature and can later return a spell from your graveyard. Hearth Elemental is two more cards that get cheaper as the graveyard fills. I left out Sunderflock, even though the Izzet Crab list runs it, because it would bounce your own Tolarian Terror.

**Mana:** I borrowed the Izzet Phoenix mana base, cut to 19 lands. The check tool flagged that this has 11 red sources, compared with about 14 in Phoenix lists. I accepted that because this deck only has 10 red cards and also needs 8 green sources. Bushwhack's land mode makes up some of the difference.

**Sideboard:** It's aimed at the top decks in the current results. Soul-Guide Lantern, Unlicensed Hearse and Pick Your Poison are for Greasefang and Cauldron. Abrade, Aether Gust and Brotherhood's End are for the red decks. Negate and Mystical Dispute are for UW Control.

T1-2: fetch a basic land (fixes the third color) and puts a sorcery in the graveyard
T2: kills an early creature; graveyard now holds 3+ instants/sorceries
T3: comes down for UU or less as a 5/5 ward 2 and starts attacking
Flashed in on the opponent's end step for 2-3 mana; on the next turn it enters... untaps and taps two blockers, so both 5/5s connect
Terror deals 5 to their best blocker or Sheoldred, keeping the path clear; 10 damage a turn ends it about two turns later
